description: The `config` object of an enabled `spiffe_identity` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component SpiffeIdentityConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

SpiffeIdentityConfig.description:
Plugin: spiffe_identity — Extracts the SPIFFE ID from the peer
certificate's URI SAN and populates `ctx.peer_spiffe_id` /
`StreamConnectionContext` metadata for downstream auth and rate-limit
plugins (notably `mesh_authz` and `rate_limiting` with
`limit_by: spiffe_identity`).

Auto-injected by mesh mode on every applicable topology; reserved
plugin id `__mesh_spiffe_identity`. Standalone usage is supported on
non-mesh gateways that still terminate mTLS and want to surface the
SPIFFE identity to other plugins.

The trust domain is admitted exactly as SPIFFE-ID section 2.1 defines
it: non-empty, at most 255 bytes, lowercase, and composed only of
`[a-z0-9.-_]` — including at the first and last byte. Userinfo, ports,
percent-encoding, and the SPIFFE ID's own 2048-byte total bound are
still enforced.

A certificate-derived peer identity is admitted as an authenticated
principal carrying the leaf certificate's `notAfter` as its
authorization deadline, so SPIFFE-only policy chains (this plugin plus
`mesh_authz`, with no `mtls_auth`) are bounded by SVID expiry on the
request, WebSocket, streaming-body, TCP+TLS, and UDP+DTLS paths. Every
request re-checks the leaf validity window, and an expired or
not-yet-valid SVID is refused with the same fixed `403`
`{"error":"invalid SPIFFE identity certificate"}` body as a malformed
one. A pre-stamped kernel-attested or HBONE-asserted `peer_spiffe_id`
carries no validity window and is not treated as certificate-bounded.

`null` and `{}` select the default extraction-only behavior: no
identity is required, every trust domain the listener's verifier
accepted is admitted, and nothing is forwarded to the backend. Every
field below is an opt-in tightening of that default.

Rejections never echo the peer certificate: a malformed SPIFFE URI SAN
is the fixed `403` `{"error":"invalid SPIFFE identity certificate"}`,
and its debug diagnostic names only a fixed reason, never the URI or
any credential its userinfo or query carried.

A proxy- or proxy-group-scoped instance on a stream proxy is refused at
admission unless that proxy sets `frontend_tls: true` and
`passthrough: false`, exactly as for `mtls_auth`. Global instances are
exempt and remain no-ops on plaintext listeners.

require_identity.description:
When true, a request or stream that reaches this plugin without a
usable SPIFFE identity (no client certificate, a certificate with
no SPIFFE URI SAN, or certificate DER that does not parse) is
refused with a fixed `403` `{"error":"SPIFFE identity required"}`.
A pre-stamped kernel-attested or HBONE-asserted identity counts as
present.

allowed_trust_domains.description:
When set, only identities whose trust domain is listed are
admitted; any other identity — certificate-derived or pre-stamped —
is refused with a fixed `403`
`{"error":"SPIFFE trust domain not allowed"}`. Entries are bare
SPIFFE trust domains (SPIFFE-ID section 2.1 grammar, no
`spiffe://` scheme), matched exactly. Omit the field to admit every
trust domain; an explicit empty list is rejected.

forward_identity.description:
When true, the admitted SPIFFE ID is forwarded to the backend in
the fixed gateway-owned request header `x-ferrum-peer-spiffe-id`
(HTTP family only). Every client-supplied copy — compared ASCII
case-insensitively with `_` read as `-` — is removed from the
initial header block before the gateway's value is set, including
on requests that carry no identity; client request-trailer copies
are dropped by the gateway's request-trailer boundary, which owns
the whole `x-ferrum-*` namespace.
